root_cause: ReprHighlighter's url regex `(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#]*)` uses an explicit allow-list character class that omits `~`, so a URL such as http://127.0.0.1/~foo stops matching at the tilde and only the prefix is styled repr.url.
best_solution: In rich/highlighter.py, ReprHighlighter.highlights, append `~` to the url pattern's character class: `[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~]*`. One-character change. Reasoning from the title alone: 'Allow tilde in URL' plus a highlighter library means a URL regex with an allow-list of characters; grep for `https|http` or `(?P<url>` to find the only URL pattern, add the missing character, and check that nothing else changes (the `#` and `?` chars were already allowed).
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_highlighter.py parametrized highlight_tests gains 3 cases for ReprHighlighter: ' http://example.org/index.html#anchor ' -> [Span(1,37,'repr.url')]; ' http://example.org/index.html?param1=value1 ' -> [Span(31,37,'repr.attrib_name'), Span(38,44,'repr.attrib_value'), Span(1,44,'repr.url')]; ' http://example.org/~folder ' -> [Span(1,27,'repr.url')]. Only the tilde case fails at base (base regex gives span (1,20)); the #anchor and ?param cases already pass at base and guard against regressions, so the fix must not change the url span semantics or the attrib_name/attrib_value spans.
locating_signals: Title 'Allow tilde in URL' names the whole fix; the body gives only 'fixes #3057' (issue text not in the statement: 'Tilde not included in link regex', print('http://127.0.0.1/~foo')). No file or function named, but in rich a grep for 'url' / 'https' leads straight to the one (?P<url>...) pattern in ReprHighlighter in rich/highlighter.py.
our_outcome_summary: Solved by all: v4, v6, v7, v8 all pass in the Kaggle env (82 tests pass in the v4 log). All four made the gold one-character change byte-for-byte. v6 also left a stray repro_tilde.py at repo root and v8 left tests/reproduce_tilde.py; both harmless here, but they are leftover scratch files in the diff. Cost grew across configs for the same patch: v4 31s/12 calls, v6 60s/22, v7 73s/33, v8 140s/92, so later configs spent up to 7.7x the calls on a trivial fix.
generalizable_lesson: When a bug says a character or token is 'not included' or 'not matched', look for an explicit allow-list character class in a regex and add only the missing character, keeping the existing order and escaping. Don't rewrite the pattern and don't widen it to \S. Hidden tests often add regression cases for nearby characters that already pass, so any wider change risks breaking them. For a one-line fix, stop once a quick repro passes: don't write scratch repro files into the repo (delete them before finishing), and cap exploration so easy tasks don't use 90+ calls.
